title: How RevisionDojo AI Feedback Works
summary: Learn how RevisionDojo AI feedback uses IB mark schemes and rubrics, what students receive, its limits, privacy controls, and when teachers matter.
body_markdown:
RevisionDojo AI feedback evaluates a submitted response against the assessment reference connected to the task. For exam-style questions, this is usually a mark scheme. For an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, or TOK essay, it is the selected assessment rubric. The system then provides marks or criterion estimates, explanations of strengths and omissions, and practical next steps.


This is **formative feedback** , which means it is intended to improve learning before final assessment. It is not official IB marking and cannot replace the professional judgment of a teacher, supervisor, moderator, or examiner.


### How RevisionDojo AI feedback works


The process can be understood in five stages:


1. **The student submits work.** This could be a written answer, calculation, diagram, timed paper, or coursework draft.
2. **The task provides context.** The chosen subject, level, paper, question, or coursework category identifies what the system should assess.
3. **The work is compared with an assessment reference.** Exam answers are considered against relevant marking requirements, while coursework is evaluated using the selected criteria and descriptors.
4. **Jojo AI produces structured feedback.** The output may include marks, annotations, criterion breakdowns, explanations, and revision priorities.
5. **The student responds to the diagnosis.** The important outcome is not the number alone, but knowing what to correct, rewrite, or practise.


This task-specific context matters because IB assessment is not based on general quality alone. An accurate paragraph may lose marks if it ignores the command term. A correct mathematical answer may also miss method marks when the required working is absent.


### How feedback differs across RevisionDojo tools


RevisionDojo does not apply one feedback format to every submission. The output depends on the activity and how the IB assesses that type of work.


RevisionDojo tool What the student submits Typical feedback


Question Bank One exam-style answer, calculation, or diagram Marks, recognized marking points, omissions, and improvement guidance


Exam Mode or online tests Responses within a timed or structured paper Question-level results, explanations, and topics requiring more practice


Coursework Grader An IA, EE, or TOK essay draft Annotations, criterion analysis, overall diagnosis, and revision priorities


Jojo AI chat A question, extract, diagram, or request for help Explanations, hints, diagnostic comments, and follow-up practice


The[RevisionDojo Question Bank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) supports repeated exam-style practice filtered by subject, level, paper, topic, and other available categories. Students can use the feedback to compare their responses with the requirements attached to each question.


[Exam Mode and mock exam workflows](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-mock-exams) extend this process across a longer attempt. A paper-level breakdown can reveal that a student understands the content but struggles with timing, command terms, or a particular question format.


The[IB Coursework Grader](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grader) addresses work that cannot be divided into isolated right or wrong answers. Its feedback is therefore organized around annotations, criteria, and broader qualities such as analysis, evaluation, communication, or reflection where relevant.


### What mark-scheme-aligned feedback means


**Mark-scheme-aligned** does not mean that the AI is an official examiner. It means the feedback attempts to follow the awarding logic associated with the question instead of applying a generic standard for good writing.


Suppose a three-mark Biology question asks a student to explain a process. The response might state one correct fact but omit the causal links needed for a complete explanation. Useful feedback distinguishes the creditworthy point from the missing reasoning that prevents full marks.


Command terms are equally important. **Describe** asks for relevant characteristics, while **evaluate** normally requires a supported judgment. Students should use the feedback to establish what earned credit, what requirement was missing, and what must change in the next independent response. RevisionDojo's guide to[effective IB practice resources and AI study tools](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/effective-ib-practice-resources-ai-study-tools) explains how this can fit into a wider practice routine.


### How coursework feedback should be interpreted


For coursework, the student must select the correct task, subject, and level where applicable. An Economics IA, Mathematics IA, subject Extended Essay, and TOK essay use different assessment frameworks, so these categories are not interchangeable.


RevisionDojo describes its coursework output as including annotations, criterion-by-criterion comments, an overall diagnosis, and targeted revisions. Its overview of[AI-powered IB coursework grading](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ai-powered-ib-coursework-grading-services) provides more detail about this draft-review process.


A criterion estimate is not a guaranteed final mark. Coursework descriptors require judgment, and an automated system may misunderstand the research context, subject conventions, supporting materials, or reasoning behind a decision. Convert broad comments into precise actions. For example, turn “improve evaluation” into “compare the reliability of the two main sources and explain how their limitations affect the conclusion.”


Students must decide whether each recommendation is accurate and appropriate. Feedback should support judgment rather than remove it.


### What the system can and cannot identify


AI feedback is useful for detecting visible features such as omitted working, unsupported claims, incomplete labels, unclear explanations, weak links to a research question, or apparent mismatches with a command term.


However, the system may:


- Misread an unconventional but valid argument.
- Miss information within a complex image, equation, table, or appendix.
- Apply a descriptor more rigidly than a human marker would.
- Respond confidently when the submission lacks context.
- Produce a mark different from a teacher's reasonable judgment.
- Improve surface wording without strengthening the underlying thinking.


Students should therefore inspect the explanation behind a score. If Jojo AI awards two marks when the student expected four, the student should identify which marking points were recognized and compare them with the original answer. Significant disagreements should be discussed with a teacher. The article on[Jojo AI as an IB study assistant](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-ai-tutor) similarly presents the tool as a source of guidance rather than an infallible authority.


### Why the feedback is not official IB marking


Official results are produced through the IB's assessment processes. RevisionDojo is an independent platform, so an AI-generated mark remains an educational estimate even when it is aligned with an IB-style mark scheme or rubric.


Students should not describe an AI score as an official predicted grade unless their school has independently made that judgment. Human examiners can recognize accepted alternatives, interpret responses as a whole, and participate in moderation and standardization. These processes cannot be reproduced by a practice score alone.


### Academic integrity and responsible use


A safe workflow is **attempt, receive feedback, verify, and revise independently** . Asking AI to identify weaknesses is different from asking it to produce assessed work.


The IB's guidance on[artificial intelligence in learning, teaching, and assessment](https://www.ibo.org/programmes/artificial-intelligence-ai-in-learning-teaching-and-assessment/) requires students to review AI output critically. The[IB Academic Integrity Policy](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/shared-resources/pdfs/academic-integrity-policy-en.pdf) explains that AI-generated text, images, or graphs incorporated into assessed work must be appropriately acknowledged and referenced.


Students should:


- Produce the original answer before requesting feedback.
- Use comments to diagnose problems, not obtain replacement paragraphs.
- Verify factual and assessment claims with trusted materials.
- Rewrite using their own reasoning and voice.
- Retain drafts, sources, and records of important decisions.
- Follow school rules on AI use and disclosure.
- Ask a teacher when the permitted boundary is unclear.


A student should be able to explain and defend every revision. If they cannot do so without consulting the AI response, the change does not yet demonstrate secure learning.


### Privacy and uploaded coursework


RevisionDojo's[coursework file privacy explanation](https://www.revisiondojo.com/help-center/coursework-file-privacy) states that the option to delete an uploaded coursework file after **48 hours** is selected by default. Reports and comments may remain after the source file expires, and users can change the deletion option before submission.


The page also explains that submitted text is sent to the providers required to perform the selected AI service. Optional writing or similarity checks may involve additional providers. RevisionDojo's[Privacy Policy](https://www.revisiondojo.com/privacy/policy) states that identifiable student work, personal information, and educational records are not used to train or fine-tune foundation AI models. The[student data and AI privacy overview](https://www.revisiondojo.com/data-and-privacy) summarizes related controls.


Before uploading, remove unnecessary names, candidate details, school identifiers, and personal information. Keep the original file securely, inspect the deletion setting, and consult the current policy because platform practices may change.


### A practical feedback cycle


Use RevisionDojo AI feedback as a repeated learning cycle:


1. Attempt the task independently under appropriate conditions.
2. Submit enough working for the method to be assessed.
3. Read the mark or criterion breakdown before the proposed correction.
4. Find evidence in the response that supports or contradicts each comment.
5. Rewrite or retry without copying generated wording.
6. Test the same skill later using a different question.
7. Consult a teacher about unresolved disagreements or high-stakes decisions.


Improved performance on a new task provides stronger evidence of learning than a higher AI score on an repeatedly edited draft.


### Conclusion


RevisionDojo AI feedback connects submitted work to the assessment context of a particular IB task, then provides marks, explanations, annotations, or criterion-level guidance. Its purpose is to identify what appears successful, what is missing, and what the student should practise next.


The output remains advisory and should be checked against course materials and teacher guidance. RevisionDojo's Question Bank, Jojo AI, Mock Exams, Coursework Grader, and Tutors are most useful within this independent, evidence-based feedback cycle.
